story.fullStory:
Nick Lowe's "Cruel To Be Kind" reached #12 on the Billboard Hot 100. "Cruel to Be Kind" is a song co-written by Nick Lowe and his former bandmate Ian Gomm while the pair were in Brinsley Schwarz.

The song only appeared as the 1978 B-side of Lowe's "Little Hitler" single until Columbia Records convinced him to rerecord it as a potential single for his 1979 album Labour of Lust.

Musically, the song was inspired by "The Love I Lost" by Harold Melvin & the Blue Notes, an influence reflected in more recent performances of the song.

The song peaked at #12 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 15 weeks on the chart.
